classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate three logarithmic curves on each set of axes using reflections, horizontal translations and dilations, and identify shifted vertical asymptotes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch on one set of axes $y=\log_5 x$, $y=\log_{\frac15}x$ and $y=\log_5(-x)$.

answer.short: See graph. All three curves have vertical asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked:
$y=\log_5x$ passes through $(1,0)$ and $(5,1)$.
$$\begin{align*}\log_{\frac15}x&=\frac{\log_5x}{\log_5(\frac15)}\\\log_{\frac15}x&=-\log_5x\end{align*}$$
Reflect $y=\log_5x$ in the $x$-axis to obtain $y=\log_{\frac15}x$, through $(1,0)$ and $(5,-1)$. Reflect $y=\log_5x$ in the $y$-axis to obtain $y=\log_5(-x)$, through $(-1,0)$ and $(-5,1)$. Each has vertical asymptote $x=0$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Sketch on one set of axes $y=\log_5x$, $y=\log_5(x-2)$, and $y=\log_5(2-x)$, and write down the asymptotes of the three graphs.

answer.short: See graph. The vertical asymptotes, in the order listed, are $x=0$, $x=2$ and $x=2$.
answer.worked:
$y=\log_5x$ passes through $(1,0)$ and $(5,1)$, with asymptote $x=0$.
Shift this graph right by $2$ units to obtain $y=\log_5(x-2)$, through $(3,0)$ and $(7,1)$, with asymptote $x=2$.
Reflect $y=\log_5x$ in the $y$-axis, then shift right by $2$ units to obtain $y=\log_5(2-x)$, through $(1,0)$ and $(-3,1)$, with asymptote $x=2$. This last curve lies to the left of its asymptote.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Sketch on one set of axes $y=\log_5x$, $y=\log_5 2x$, and $y=2\log_5x-2$.

answer.short: See graph. The $x$-intercepts, in the order listed, are $1$, $\frac12$ and $5$; all three have vertical asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked:
Start with $y=\log_5x$, through $(1,0)$ and $(5,1)$.
A horizontal dilation of factor $\frac12$ gives $y=\log_5(2x)$, through $(\frac12,0)$ and $(\frac52,1)$.
A vertical dilation of factor $2$, followed by a shift down $2$ units, gives $y=2\log_5x-2$, through $(1,-2)$ and $(5,0)$. All three curves increase on $x>0$ and have vertical asymptote $x=0$.
